summary: Self-referencing dependency resolves from plain-HTTP non-registry host, delivering arbitrary code on install
details: package.json declares the package's own name in both dependencies and devDependencies pointing at http://pack.nppacks.com/npm/react-remove-properties — a plain-HTTP, non-npm-registry, unpinned URL. On `npm install`, npm fetches and installs whatever tarball is served at that mutable third-party endpoint into the installer's node_modules, giving the operator of pack.nppacks.com arbitrary-code delivery into the install. The source is not the official registry, the transport is cleartext HTTP (trivially MITM-able on any network path), the resolution is unpinned (no integrity/hash), and the host is outside npm's audit surface. A header comment in index.js labels the package as 'Security Research Testing Purpose,' but a self-label does not change the delivery mechanism.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
